solution:
A function \(f\) is a p.d.f. of a continuous r.v. only if BOTH conditions hold:
(1) \(f(x) \geq 0\) for every \(x\), and
(2) the total area under \(f\) is 1.
Condition (1): for \(0 \leq x \leq \dfrac{\pi}{2}\) we have \(\sin x \geq 0\), so \(f(x) \geq 0\) throughout the support.
Condition (2):
\(\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin x \, dx = \Big[-\cos x\Big]_{0}^{\pi/2} = -\cos\dfrac{\pi}{2} + \cos 0 = 0 + 1 = 1\)
Both conditions are satisfied.
\(\therefore f(x) = \sin x\), \(0 \leq x \leq \dfrac{\pi}{2}\), IS a p.d.f. of the r.v. \(X\).

[Textbook answer-key error: the key says "Not a p.d.f.", but it is one. The function is the standard triangular density: \(\int_{0}^{1}x\,dx=1/2\) and \(\int_{1}^{2}(2-x)\,dx=1/2\), totalling exactly 1, and it is non-negative throughout its support (its minimum on each branch is 0). Both defining conditions hold.]

Here \(f(x) = x\) on \(0 \leq x \leq 1\) and \(f(x) = 2 - x\) on \(1 < x < 2\).
Condition (1), non-negativity: on \([0, 1]\), \(x \geq 0\); on \((1, 2)\), \(x < 2\) so \(2 - x > 0\). Hence \(f(x) \geq 0\) on the whole support.
Condition (2), total area. The rule changes at \(x = 1\), so split the integral there:
\(\int_{0}^{1} x \, dx = \left[\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\right]_{0}^{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\)
\(\int_{1}^{2} (2 - x) \, dx = \left[2x - \dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\right]_{1}^{2} = (4 - 2) - \left(2 - \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 2 - \dfrac{3}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\)
Total area \(= \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} = 1\)
Both conditions are satisfied.
\(\therefore\) this \(f\) IS a p.d.f. of the r.v. \(X\). (It is the triangular density on \([0, 2]\) rising to a peak at \(x = 1\).)

Condition (1), non-negativity: \(f(x) = 2 > 0\) on \(0 \leq x \leq 1\), so this condition holds.
Condition (2), total area:
\(\int_{0}^{1} 2 \, dx = \Big[2x\Big]_{0}^{1} = 2 - 0 = 2\)
The total area is 2, not 1, so condition (2) FAILS.
\(\therefore f(x) = 2\), \(0 \leq x \leq 1\), is NOT a p.d.f. of a r.v.
Note: being non-negative is never enough by itself; the total area must be exactly 1. The same constant would work as a p.d.f. if the support were halved, i.e. \(f(x) = 2\) on \(0 \leq x \leq \dfrac{1}{2}\), or if the value were halved, i.e. \(f(x) = 1\) on \(0 \leq x \leq 1\).

Here \(f(x) = \dfrac{x}{8}\) for \(0 < x < 4\) and \(f(x) = 0\) otherwise. (Check: \(f \geq 0\) on \((0,4)\) and \(\int_{0}^{4} \dfrac{x}{8}\, dx = \left[\dfrac{x^{2}}{16}\right]_{0}^{4} = 1\), so it is a genuine p.d.f.)
Since \(f(x) = 0\) for \(x \leq 0\), only the part of the event lying inside \((0, 4)\) contributes:
\(P(X < 1.5) = \int_{0}^{1.5} \dfrac{x}{8}\, dx = \left[\dfrac{x^{2}}{16}\right]_{0}^{1.5} = \dfrac{(1.5)^{2}}{16} = \dfrac{2.25}{16}\)
\(\therefore P(X < 1.5) = \dfrac{9}{64} = 0.140625\)

Here \(f(x) = \dfrac{x}{8}\) for \(0 < x < 4\) and \(f(x) = 0\) otherwise. The interval \((1, 2)\) lies entirely inside the support, so
\(P(1 < X < 2) = \int_{1}^{2} \dfrac{x}{8}\, dx = \left[\dfrac{x^{2}}{16}\right]_{1}^{2} = \dfrac{4}{16} - \dfrac{1}{16} = \dfrac{3}{16}\)
\(\therefore P(1 < X < 2) = \dfrac{3}{16} = 0.1875\)

Here \(f(x) = \dfrac{x}{8}\) for \(0 < x < 4\) and \(f(x) = 0\) otherwise. The event \(X > 2\) contributes only over \((2, 4)\), because \(f\) vanishes beyond \(x = 4\):
\(P(X > 2) = \int_{2}^{4} \dfrac{x}{8}\, dx = \left[\dfrac{x^{2}}{16}\right]_{2}^{4} = \dfrac{16}{16} - \dfrac{4}{16} = \dfrac{12}{16}\)
\(\therefore P(X > 2) = \dfrac{3}{4} = 0.75\)
Check by complement: \(P(X \leq 2) = \dfrac{2^{2}}{16} = \dfrac{1}{4}\), and \(1 - \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{3}{4}\). (For a continuous r.v. \(P(X = 2) = 0\), so \(P(X \leq 2)\) and \(P(X < 2)\) are the same number.)

Test both requirements for a p.d.f.
Condition (1), non-negativity: \(f(x) = \dfrac{x^{2}}{3}\) and \(x^{2} \geq 0\) for every real \(x\), so \(f(x) \geq 0\) on \(-1 < x < 2\). (Part of the support is negative, but it is \(x\) that is negative there, never \(f(x)\).)
Condition (2), total area:
\(\int_{-1}^{2} \dfrac{x^{2}}{3}\, dx = \left[\dfrac{x^{3}}{9}\right]_{-1}^{2} = \dfrac{8}{9} - \left(\dfrac{-1}{9}\right) = \dfrac{8}{9} + \dfrac{1}{9} = 1\)
Both conditions hold.
\(\therefore f(x) = \dfrac{x^{2}}{3}\), \(-1 < x < 2\), IS a p.d.f. of the r.v. \(X\).

With \(f(x) = \dfrac{x^{2}}{3}\) on \(-1 < x < 2\):
\(P(0 < X \leq 1) = \int_{0}^{1} \dfrac{x^{2}}{3}\, dx = \left[\dfrac{x^{3}}{9}\right]_{0}^{1} = \dfrac{1}{9} - 0\)
\(\therefore P(0 < X \leq 1) = \dfrac{1}{9} \approx 0.1111\)
(The endpoint \(x = 1\) is included as printed, but for a continuous r.v. \(P(X = 1) = 0\), so including or excluding it does not change the value.)

"\(X\) is negative" is the event \(X < 0\). The p.d.f. is zero below \(x = -1\), so the integral runs only from \(-1\) to \(0\):
\(P(X < 0) = \int_{-1}^{0} \dfrac{x^{2}}{3}\, dx = \left[\dfrac{x^{3}}{9}\right]_{-1}^{0} = 0 - \left(\dfrac{-1}{9}\right) = \dfrac{1}{9}\)
\(\therefore P(X < 0) = \dfrac{1}{9} \approx 0.1111\)

The constant \(k\) is precisely what makes the total area 1 (the function as printed is deliberately unnormalised until \(k\) is found).
\(\int_{0}^{2} kx \, dx = 1\)
\(k\left[\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\right]_{0}^{2} = 1 \Rightarrow k\left(\dfrac{4}{2} - 0\right) = 1 \Rightarrow 2k = 1\)
\(\therefore k = \dfrac{1}{2}\)
Since \(k > 0\) and \(x > 0\) on the support, \(f(x) = \dfrac{x}{2} \geq 0\) there, so the non-negativity condition holds too.
Now \(f(x) = \dfrac{x}{2}\) for \(0 < x < 2\), and \(\left(\dfrac{1}{4}, \dfrac{3}{2}\right)\) lies inside the support:
\(P\left(\dfrac{1}{4} < X < \dfrac{3}{2}\right) = \int_{1/4}^{3/2} \dfrac{x}{2}\, dx = \left[\dfrac{x^{2}}{4}\right]_{1/4}^{3/2} = \dfrac{9/4}{4} - \dfrac{1/16}{4} = \dfrac{9}{16} - \dfrac{1}{64}\)
\(= \dfrac{36 - 1}{64} = \dfrac{35}{64}\)
\(\therefore k = \dfrac{1}{2}\) and \(P\left(\dfrac{1}{4} < X < \dfrac{3}{2}\right) = \dfrac{35}{64} = 0.546875\)

Find \(k\) from the total-area condition:
\(\int_{0}^{1} kx(1 - x)\, dx = 1\)
\(k\int_{0}^{1} (x - x^{2})\, dx = k\left[\dfrac{x^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{x^{3}}{3}\right]_{0}^{1} = k\left(\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{3}\right) = \dfrac{k}{6} = 1\)
\(\therefore k = 6\)
Since \(k > 0\) and \(x(1 - x) \geq 0\) for \(0 < x < 1\), the non-negativity condition also holds.
So \(f(x) = 6x(1 - x) = 6x - 6x^{2}\), whose antiderivative is \(3x^{2} - 2x^{3}\).
Values of \(3x^{2} - 2x^{3}\):
at \(x = \dfrac{1}{2}\): \(3\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right) - 2\left(\dfrac{1}{8}\right) = \dfrac{3}{4} - \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}\)
at \(x = \dfrac{1}{4}\): \(3\left(\dfrac{1}{16}\right) - 2\left(\dfrac{1}{64}\right) = \dfrac{3}{16} - \dfrac{1}{32} = \dfrac{5}{32}\)
at \(x = 0\): \(0\)
Hence
\(P\left(\dfrac{1}{4} < X < \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{5}{32} = \dfrac{16 - 5}{32} = \dfrac{11}{32}\)
\(P\left(X < \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2} - 0 = \dfrac{1}{2}\)
\(\therefore k = 6\), \(P\left(\dfrac{1}{4} < X < \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{11}{32} = 0.34375\), \(P\left(X < \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\).
(The second answer is a useful check: \(f\) is symmetric about \(x = \dfrac{1}{2}\), so exactly half the area lies on each side of it.)

Here \(f(x) = 0.5x = \dfrac{x}{2}\) for \(0 \leq x \leq 2\) and \(f(x) = 0\) otherwise. (Check: \(f \geq 0\) there and \(\int_{0}^{2} \dfrac{x}{2}\, dx = \left[\dfrac{x^{2}}{4}\right]_{0}^{2} = 1\).)
\(P(X \leq 1) = \int_{0}^{1} \dfrac{x}{2}\, dx = \left[\dfrac{x^{2}}{4}\right]_{0}^{1} = \dfrac{1}{4}\)
\(\therefore P(X \leq 1) = \dfrac{1}{4} = 0.25\)
(\(X\) is continuous, so \(P(X = 1) = 0\); hence \(P(X \leq 1)\) and \(P(X < 1)\) are the same number.)

With \(f(x) = \dfrac{x}{2}\) on \(0 \leq x \leq 2\) and \(0\) beyond \(x = 2\), the event \(X \geq 1.5\) contributes only over \([1.5, 2]\):
\(P(X \geq 1.5) = \int_{1.5}^{2} \dfrac{x}{2}\, dx = \left[\dfrac{x^{2}}{4}\right]_{1.5}^{2} = \dfrac{4}{4} - \dfrac{2.25}{4} = \dfrac{1.75}{4}\)
\(\therefore P(X \geq 1.5) = \dfrac{7}{16} = 0.4375\)
Check by complement: \(P(X < 1.5) = \dfrac{(1.5)^{2}}{4} = \dfrac{2.25}{4} = 0.5625\), and \(1 - 0.5625 = 0.4375\).

Here \(f(x) = \dfrac{1}{5}\) for \(0 \leq x \leq 5\) and \(0\) otherwise: the waiting time is uniformly distributed over 5 minutes. (Check: \(f > 0\) and \(\int_{0}^{5} \dfrac{1}{5}\, dx = 1\).)
\(P(1 < X < 3) = \int_{1}^{3} \dfrac{1}{5}\, dx = \left[\dfrac{x}{5}\right]_{1}^{3} = \dfrac{3}{5} - \dfrac{1}{5} = \dfrac{2}{5}\)
\(\therefore\) the probability that the waiting time is between 1 and 3 minutes is \(\dfrac{2}{5} = 0.4\).
(For a uniform density this is just the length of the interval divided by the length of the support: \(\dfrac{3 - 1}{5}\).)

With \(f(x) = \dfrac{1}{5}\) on \(0 \leq x \leq 5\), the event \(X > 4\) contributes only over \((4, 5]\), since \(f = 0\) beyond 5 minutes:
\(P(X > 4) = \int_{4}^{5} \dfrac{1}{5}\, dx = \left[\dfrac{x}{5}\right]_{4}^{5} = 1 - \dfrac{4}{5} = \dfrac{1}{5}\)
\(\therefore\) the probability that the waiting time is more than 4 minutes is \(\dfrac{1}{5} = 0.2\).

First find \(k\) from the total-area condition:
\(\int_{-2}^{2} k(4 - x^{2})\, dx = 1\)
\(k\left[4x - \dfrac{x^{3}}{3}\right]_{-2}^{2} = k\left[\left(8 - \dfrac{8}{3}\right) - \left(-8 + \dfrac{8}{3}\right)\right] = k\left(16 - \dfrac{16}{3}\right) = \dfrac{32k}{3} = 1\)
\(\therefore k = \dfrac{3}{32}\)
Since \(k > 0\) and \(4 - x^{2} \geq 0\) for \(-2 \leq x \leq 2\), the non-negativity condition holds as well, so \(f\) is a genuine p.d.f.
Now
\(P(X > 0) = \int_{0}^{2} \dfrac{3}{32}(4 - x^{2})\, dx = \dfrac{3}{32}\left[4x - \dfrac{x^{3}}{3}\right]_{0}^{2} = \dfrac{3}{32}\left(8 - \dfrac{8}{3}\right) = \dfrac{3}{32} \times \dfrac{16}{3}\)
\(\therefore P(X > 0) = \dfrac{1}{2}\)
This is exactly what symmetry predicts: \(f(-x) = f(x)\), so the area splits equally about \(x = 0\).

From the total-area condition \(\int_{-2}^{2} k(4 - x^{2})\, dx = \dfrac{32k}{3} = 1\), so \(k = \dfrac{3}{32}\).
\(P(-1 < X < 1) = \dfrac{3}{32}\int_{-1}^{1} (4 - x^{2})\, dx = \dfrac{3}{32}\left[4x - \dfrac{x^{3}}{3}\right]_{-1}^{1}\)
\(= \dfrac{3}{32}\left[\left(4 - \dfrac{1}{3}\right) - \left(-4 + \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\right] = \dfrac{3}{32}\left(8 - \dfrac{2}{3}\right) = \dfrac{3}{32} \times \dfrac{22}{3} = \dfrac{22}{32}\)
\(\therefore P(-1 < X < 1) = \dfrac{11}{16} = 0.6875\)

A note on the statement: as printed, the two conditions \(-0.5 < x\) and \(x > 0.5\) overlap, because every \(x\) greater than \(0.5\) is automatically greater than \(-0.5\); their literal union is just \(x > -0.5\). The event plainly intended is the pair of TAILS, \(X < -0.5\) or \(X > 0.5\), i.e. the error exceeds \(0.5\) in magnitude. The intended reading is solved first.
As before, \(k = \dfrac{3}{32}\), so \(f(x) = \dfrac{3}{32}(4 - x^{2})\) on \([-2, 2]\).
Middle piece:
\(P(-0.5 < X < 0.5) = \dfrac{3}{32}\left[4x - \dfrac{x^{3}}{3}\right]_{-0.5}^{0.5} = \dfrac{3}{32}\left[\left(2 - \dfrac{1}{24}\right) - \left(-2 + \dfrac{1}{24}\right)\right] = \dfrac{3}{32}\left(4 - \dfrac{1}{12}\right)\)
\(= \dfrac{3}{32} \times \dfrac{47}{12} = \dfrac{47}{128}\)
Intended reading (the two tails), by complement:
\(P(X < -0.5 \text{ or } X > 0.5) = 1 - \dfrac{47}{128} = \dfrac{81}{128}\)
\(\therefore\) the required probability is \(\dfrac{81}{128} = 0.6328125\).
Literal reading, for completeness: \(P(X > -0.5) = 1 - P(X < -0.5)\), and by symmetry \(P(X < -0.5) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{81}{128}\right) = \dfrac{81}{256}\), so \(P(X > -0.5) = \dfrac{175}{256} = 0.68359375\).

The c.d.f. is \(F(x) = P(X \leq x) = \int_{-\infty}^{x} f(t)\, dt\), which here means integrating from the lower end of the support, \(t = 0\).
For \(x \leq 0\): \(f = 0\) throughout, so \(F(x) = 0\).
For \(0 < x < 4\):
\(F(x) = \int_{0}^{x} \dfrac{t}{8}\, dt = \left[\dfrac{t^{2}}{16}\right]_{0}^{x} = \dfrac{x^{2}}{16}\)
For \(x \geq 4\): all the area has been accumulated, so \(F(x) = \dfrac{4^{2}}{16} = 1\).
\(\therefore\)
\(F(x) = 0\), for \(x \leq 0\)
\(F(x) = \dfrac{x^{2}}{16}\), for \(0 < x < 4\)
\(F(x) = 1\), for \(x \geq 4\)
The expression is continuous at both joins (\(F \to 0\) as \(x \to 0^{+}\) and \(F \to 1\) as \(x \to 4^{-}\)) and non-decreasing, as a c.d.f. must be.

The support is \(-1 < x < 2\), so the c.d.f. accumulates area starting at \(t = -1\).
For \(x \leq -1\): \(F(x) = 0\).
For \(-1 < x < 2\):
\(F(x) = \int_{-1}^{x} \dfrac{t^{2}}{3}\, dt = \left[\dfrac{t^{3}}{9}\right]_{-1}^{x} = \dfrac{x^{3}}{9} - \left(\dfrac{-1}{9}\right) = \dfrac{x^{3} + 1}{9}\)
For \(x \geq 2\): \(F(x) = \dfrac{8 + 1}{9} = 1\).
\(\therefore\)
\(F(x) = 0\), for \(x \leq -1\)
\(F(x) = \dfrac{x^{3} + 1}{9}\), for \(-1 < x < 2\)
\(F(x) = 1\), for \(x \geq 2\)
Now read the required probabilities off \(F\).
\(P(X < 1) = F(1) = \dfrac{1 + 1}{9} = \dfrac{2}{9}\)
\(P(X < -2) = F(-2) = 0\), since \(-2\) is below the support (the error can never be that small).
\(P(X > 0) = 1 - F(0) = 1 - \dfrac{0 + 1}{9} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{9} = \dfrac{8}{9}\)
\(P(1 < X < 2) = F(2) - F(1) = 1 - \dfrac{2}{9} = \dfrac{7}{9}\)
\(\therefore P(X < 1) = \dfrac{2}{9}\), \(P(X < -2) = 0\), \(P(X > 0) = \dfrac{8}{9}\), \(P(1 < X < 2) = \dfrac{7}{9}\).
(Because \(X\) is continuous, \(P(X = c) = 0\) at every single point, so strict and non-strict inequalities give the same values here.)

[Textbook answer-key error: the key prints \(4/\log 3\) in the \(E(X)\) slot, but that is \(E(X^{2})\). \(E(X)=2c=2/\log 3=1.82048\); \(E(X^{2})=4c=3.64096\). Two proofs: the support is \((1,3)\) so the mean must lie inside it, and \(3.641>3\); and the key's own variance reconciles only with \(E(X)=2/\log 3\) — using its printed middle value gives a variance of \(-9.6156\), which is impossible. The values of \(c\) and of the variance are correct.]

Find \(c\) from the total-area condition (throughout, \(\log\) means the natural logarithm):
\(\int_{1}^{3} \dfrac{c}{x}\, dx = 1\)
\(c\Big[\log x\Big]_{1}^{3} = c(\log 3 - \log 1) = c\log 3 = 1\)
\(\therefore c = \dfrac{1}{\log 3} \approx 0.9102\)
Since \(c > 0\) and \(x > 0\) on the support, \(f(x) = \dfrac{c}{x} > 0\) there, so the non-negativity condition also holds.
Mean:
\(E(X) = \int_{1}^{3} x \cdot \dfrac{c}{x}\, dx = c\int_{1}^{3} 1 \, dx = c(3 - 1) = 2c\)
\(\therefore E(X) = \dfrac{2}{\log 3} \approx 1.8205\)
Second moment:
\(E(X^{2}) = \int_{1}^{3} x^{2} \cdot \dfrac{c}{x}\, dx = c\int_{1}^{3} x \, dx = c\left[\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\right]_{1}^{3} = c\left(\dfrac{9}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 4c = \dfrac{4}{\log 3}\)
Variance:
\(\mathrm{Var}(X) = E(X^{2}) - \big[E(X)\big]^{2} = \dfrac{4}{\log 3} - \left(\dfrac{2}{\log 3}\right)^{2} = \dfrac{4}{\log 3} - \dfrac{4}{(\log 3)^{2}}\)
\(= \dfrac{4(\log 3 - 1)}{(\log 3)^{2}}\)
\(\therefore c = \dfrac{1}{\log 3}\), \(E(X) = \dfrac{2}{\log 3} \approx 1.8205\), \(\mathrm{Var}(X) = \dfrac{4(\log 3 - 1)}{(\log 3)^{2}} \approx 0.3268\).
(The mean lies inside \((1, 3)\) and the variance is positive, as they must be.)
